DIAGNOSIS READY: Neonatal Herpes Simplex Virus (HSV) Infection

The clinical picture of a generalized erythematous maculopapular rash with pustules, sparing the palms and soles, in a 4-day-old newborn is highly specific for disseminated or cutaneous HSV. Despite the maternal history of gonorrhea, the rash morphology and distribution strongly favor HSV over gonococcal infection. We await the final Gram stain and image results to rule out bacterial superinfection, but the primary diagnosis is HSV.
